implemented_change: Iterator implementations must establish their yielded-item predicate and preserve it for future items. Flux retains valid iterator-input refinements when Map::next checks its callback. Mapped ranges now verify input preconditions, output index bounds, and those bounds across loops.
mechanism: Trusted extern methods may refine inherited impl predicates using receiver state. Exact Rust predicate matching is preserved. Metadata records replaced parent indices; callers check the replacements and retain other inherited callback obligations. Range::step records start advancement and the shared end bound.
trust_boundary: The Map and Range contracts are reviewed standard-library models. Client proofs are checked against those models; arbitrary summary inference and tuple-index inference are not implemented by this layer.
source_patch_scope: Codex source was clean at the base revision for both selected checks. The temporary parser candidate has its own patch hash and was restored before writing this ledger.

integration.metadata_compatibility: Rebuild pre-change Flux metadata. The verifier detected and rejected a stale flux-rs artifact during development; the final suite used rebuilt models.

positive_cases: two-callback extern method with one inherited bound refined
negative_cases: false assertion in a mapped loop
false Some result for an empty range
local method cannot override inherited predicates through the extern mechanism
validation.performance_note: Uncached uses an empty proof-cache namespace with populated Cargo build caches. Cached selected checks execute zero solver queries. End-to-end times include compilation and setup; this single comparison makes no overall speedup claim.

soundness_audit.counterexample: A custom iterator yields 7 while declaring valid_item = false; the unchecked predicate made a false assertion in its consumer verify.
soundness_audit.native_result: The mapped iterator yields [7], confirming its body is reachable.

before_fix.status: false assertion accepted in both cases

fixed_obligations: next establishes valid_item for every returned Some payload
every item valid in the next state is valid in the previous state
item obligations apply even without an exact-size model
regressions: false item predicates with and without size models are rejected
a changing next-item-only predicate is rejected
constant item predicates and a shrinking countdown envelope verify
generic bool/char item types retain reachable branches
soundness_audit.smt_precision: Unsupported positive quantified assumptions are dropped conservatively. Quantified heads are still proved; unproved quantified requirements are rejected.
soundness_audit.associated_sorts: Predicate declarations instantiate actual generic arguments and normalize associated Item sorts; this fixes the bool-item solver crash exposed by the item contract.

diagnostics: The final map cannot establish the returned index bound.
Nested callbacks have unresolved no-panic obligations for str::find and Ordering::then_with.
parser_candidate.next_work: Carry enumerated tuple indices and callback result refinements through filter_map and min_by, then retry the same caller obligation. Resolve callback panic models without weakening the index requirement.
